title: The Wrath of Achilles
text:
In the tenth year of the siege of Troy, Chryses, a priest of Apollo, came to the Greek camp with a rich ransom for his daughter Chryseis, whom Agamemnon, the commander in chief, had taken as a prize of war. Agamemnon sent him away with insults. Apollo answered his priest's prayer with a plague, and for nine days the funeral pyres burned.

Achilles, the greatest of the Greek warriors, called an assembly. The seer Calchas revealed the cause, and Agamemnon was forced to give the girl back. But he would not go without a prize while others kept theirs. He announced that he would take Briseis, the woman Achilles had been awarded by the army.

Achilles was so enraged that he began to draw his sword, and only the goddess Athena, seizing him by the hair, held him back. Instead he swore that the Greeks would one day long for him when they were falling in hundreds before Hector, and he withdrew to his ships with his men. Agamemnon's heralds took Briseis from his tent.

Achilles then asked his mother, the sea goddess Thetis, to persuade Zeus to give the Trojans victory until the Greeks honored him. Zeus agreed. In the fighting that followed, the Greeks were driven back to their ships, and Achilles' dearest friend Patroclus was killed.
lesson: Insulting your best people to protect your own pride can cost far more than the prize you keep. When you are wrong in front of everyone, give way gracefully instead of making someone else pay.
